description: Sulfur is a chemical element with symbol S and atomic number 16. It is abundant, multivalent and nonmetallic, forming cyclic octatomic molecules with the formula S8 under normal conditions. Elemental sulfur is a bright yellow, crystalline solid at room temperature.
uses: The greatest commercial use of sulfur is the production of sulfuric acid for sulfate and phosphate fertilizers and other chemical processes. It is also used in matches, insecticides, and fungicides. Sulfur is an essential element for all life, appearing in amino acids such as cysteine and methionine, vitamins like biotin and thiamine, and cofactors including glutathione and iron-sulfur proteins.
characteristics: Octasulfur is a soft, bright-yellow solid that is odorless, melting at 115.21°C and boiling at 444.6°C. It has a density of about 2 g/cm³ and all stable allotropes are excellent electrical insulators. Sulfur is insoluble in water but soluble in carbon disulfide and other nonpolar organic solvents, and it reacts with nearly all other elements except noble gases.
